title: Cybersecurity Concepts: CIA, AAA, Non-Repudiation and Privacy

header.html: 1.1 Understand cybersecurity concepts: Confidentiality; Integrity; Availability; Authentication, Authorization, Accounting (AAA); Non-repudiation; Privacy
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1The CIA triad

Goal Meaning Example controls Attack that breaks it
Confidentiality Only authorized people can read the data Encryption, access control, data classification Disclosure: a data breach, eavesdropping
Integrity Data is accurate and unaltered Hashing, digital signatures, version control, input checks Alteration: tampering, model poisoning
Availability Systems and data are there when needed Redundancy, backups, patching, DDoS protection Destruction or denial: ransomware, DDoS

The opposite of CIA is DAD: Disclosure, Alteration, Destruction (or denial).

Exam tip

. Match the goal to the symptom. Leak = confidentiality. Changed or fake data = integrity. Outage = availability. A hash proves integrity, not secrecy.

2AI and the triad

Foundational AI concepts are part of the outline in every domain.

Goal AI example
Confidentiality Protect the privacy of training data; staff must not paste secrets into public AI tools
Integrity Prevent model poisoning by controlling the training data
Availability A model or its service that is down or degraded hurts operations

3AAA: authentication, authorization, accounting

Step Question Examples
Authentication Who are you? Password, token, fingerprint, multi-factor authentication (MFA)
Authorization What may you do? Permissions, roles, access control lists
Accounting What did you do? Logs, audit trails, session records

Authentication factors: something you know (password, PIN), something you have (token, smart card, phone), something you are (fingerprint, face). MFA uses factors from two or more different categories; two passwords are not MFA.

Exam tip

. Authentication comes first, then authorization, then accounting. Logs support accountability because they tie actions to an identity.

4Non-repudiation

Non-repudiation means a person cannot credibly deny an action such as sending a message or approving a payment.

Tool How it supports non-repudiation
Digital signature Proves who signed and that the data was not changed (made with the sender's private key)
Audit logs Tie the action to an identity and a time
Strong authentication Makes it hard to claim that someone else acted

AAA and non-repudiation also keep actions of AI tools traceable.

5Privacy

Privacy is the right of individuals to control how their personal information is collected, used and shared. Security protects the data; privacy decides what may be done with it.

Term Meaning
Personally identifiable information (PII) Data that identifies a person, alone or combined (name, ID number, email)
Data minimization Collect and keep only what is needed
Consent and purpose Use data only for the stated purpose
Privacy laws For example GDPR; they set duties and fines (Module 3)
Exam tip

. Security without privacy is possible; privacy without security is not. A system can be secure and still misuse personal data.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A laptop with customer records is stolen and the disk is not encrypted. Which security goal is most directly harmed?

  • AIntegrity, because the records may have been changed
  • BConfidentiality, because unauthorized people can read the data
  • CAvailability, because the staff cannot use the laptop
  • DNon-repudiation, because the owner can deny the loss
Show the answer

Answer: B. Unauthorized disclosure of data harms confidentiality; encryption would have protected it.

S2An attacker changes the amount of a bank transfer while it travels over the network. Which goal does this attack violate?

  • AConfidentiality, because the transfer was visible to others
  • BIntegrity, because the data was altered in transit
  • CAvailability, because the transfer was delayed
  • DAccountability, because the logs were turned off
Show the answer

Answer: B. Unauthorized alteration violates integrity.

S3A hospital system is encrypted by ransomware and doctors cannot open patient files. Which goal is harmed first?

  • AIntegrity, because the files were rewritten
  • BAvailability, because the data cannot be accessed
  • CPrivacy, because patient data may be shared
  • DConfidentiality, because the files were encrypted
Show the answer

Answer: B. Ransomware denies access to the data, which is an availability failure.

S4A user logs in with a password and then approves a prompt on a phone. What does this illustrate?

  • ASingle sign-on across two different systems
  • BAuthorization with two different roles
  • CMulti-factor authentication with two different factors
  • DAccounting with two separate log entries
Show the answer

Answer: C. A password (know) plus a phone (have) are two categories of factor.

S5A manager signs a contract with a digital signature and later says she never signed it. Which concept makes the denial hard to defend?

  • AAvailability of the signing service
  • BNon-repudiation provided by the signature
  • CData minimization of the contract
  • DConfidentiality of the signing key
Show the answer

Answer: B. A digital signature supports non-repudiation: the signer cannot credibly deny it.

S6A company encrypts customer data but uses it for marketing without the customers' knowledge. Which concept is violated?

  • AIntegrity, because the data was encrypted
  • BAvailability, because the data is stored
  • CPrivacy, because the data is used beyond its stated purpose
  • DAuthentication, because the data has no password
Show the answer

Answer: C. Privacy is about how personal data is used and shared, even when it is well protected.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does the C in CIA stand for?

Show the answer

Confidentiality.

R2Which control mainly supports integrity?

Show the answer

Hashing (and digital signatures).

R3What question does authorization answer?

Show the answer

What may you do?

R4Name the three authentication factor categories.

Show the answer

Something you know, have and are.

R5What does DAD stand for?

Show the answer

Disclosure, alteration, destruction (or denial).

R6What does non-repudiation prevent?

Show the answer

A person denying an action they took.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
CIA confidentiality (secrecy), integrity (accuracy), availability (access)
DAD disclosure, alteration, destruction or denial
AAA authentication (who), authorization (what), accounting (what you did)
MFA two or more different factor categories
Non-repudiation digital signatures and logs; no credible denial
Privacy control over personal data; PII; data minimization
